extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, institutional research administrators, and grant applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: A news-summary page listing recent NIH extramural policy, process, and resource updates relevant to grant applicants and awardees. It flags topics investigators should attend to (e.g., new application formats, data-sharing requirements, review-process changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection for research (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions; NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches and encourages those that enhance human relevance and translational potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will accept diverse, scientifically sound model choices but expects justification tied to the research question and translational relevance. Emphasis on human relevance and translational potential suggests applicants should explain why chosen models are the best fit; avoid choosing models that are less relevant to the question solely for convenience or precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to PF5 Collaborative International Research Project application format and features
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use the PF5-specific application format and understand PF5 award structure. Be aware that applications might be administratively split into linked awards after peer review and prior to Just-in-Time (JIT) requests — plan collaborators, budgets, and institutional commitments accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified by NIH. Applicants should consult the new format/resource to ensure compliance; failure to follow the required elements may lead to nonconformance with NIH expectations for data management and sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in research
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances a commitment to replication and reproducibility; NIH launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider and, where appropriate, incorporate replication and reproducibility practices into study design, analysis plans, and resource sharing. Highlighting replication/reproducibility efforts may align proposals with NIH priorities. Emphasize study reliability, transparent methods, and plans for verification where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand review score categories and the 'Competitive But Not Discussed' designation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH implemented emergency modifications recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cutoff; the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should understand that not all competitively scored applications are discussed; a score or percentile cutoff (historically ~33%) may determine discussion. If your application receives 'competitive but not discussed,' consider resubmission strategies, addressing reviewer comments, and consulting program staff for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate effects of centralized NIH peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralization of peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) is intended to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency in NIH peer review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should anticipate procedural changes stemming from centralized review — e.g., possible changes in study section assignment, review timelines, or evaluation practices — and monitor NIH communications for operational details. Adjust submission planning and expectations accordingly.
